title: Petrobras Stock After Q3 Earnings - Buy, Sell or Hold for Now? - The Globe and Mail
content: Brazil's state-run energy giant Petroleo Brasileiro S.A., better known as PetrobrasPBR, not only produced more oil and gas but also earned more than a year earlier in the third quarter of 2026. It also raised its annual production and cash-flow forecasts. Those are good reasons to look at the stock, even after its sharp rise this year. There are reasons for caution, too, as profit declined from the second quarter, while spending increased. For investors wondering whether to buy, the question is how much of the expected improvement is already priced in. Petrobras reported revenues of $33 billion, up 40.4% from a year earlier. Profit attributable to shareholders rose 28.4% to $7.7 billion. Excluding one-off items, profit increased 78% to $9.3 billion. Operating cash flow reached $12 billion, up 22%, while free cash flow rose 33.2% to $6.6 billion. Free cash flow measures what remains after investment spending. The stock has already rewarded investors. PBR shares have gained 54.8% in 2026 compared with 41.8% for ExxonMobil HoldingsXOM and 44.3% for ChevronCVX. A large gain alone does not tell us whether a stock is expensive, but it makes the earnings outlook worth examining closely. The results were weaker than the second quarter. Reported shareholder profit fell 25.8%, while profit excluding one-off items declined 15.9%. Lower oil prices hurt earnings, as did higher expenses. Investors should keep that comparison in mind when assessing the much stronger annual numbers. Petrobras produced a record 3.512 million barrels of oil equivalent per day (MMBOE/d) during the quarter. Refineries ran at 99% of capacity, and diesel production reached a record 769,000 barrels daily. Management now expects annual production of 3.3–3.4 MMBOE/d, up from 3.1 million. Offshore platforms are reaching higher output sooner, and the P-79 platform started earlier than planned. Petrobras also raised its operating cash-flow forecast to $45-$50 billion from $35 billion. That forecast uses higher production and revised oil-price assumptions, so the increase does not come entirely from operating improvements. ExxonMobil reported production growth in Guyana and the Permian, excluding Middle East effects, while Chevron increased capacity at existing facilities. For Petrobras, the same basic test applies: does spending lead to more production and enough cash to justify the cost? Fourth-quarter production faces scheduled maintenance and a lower Petrobras share of output under the Búzios production-sharing agreement. Investors should not assume production will rise every quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Petrobras’ 2026 earnings is $4.95 per share, up 76.8% from $2.80 in 2025. That expected increase gives the share-price rally some support. The forecast still depends on production, costs and oil prices, and it should be treated as an expectation rather than money already earned. PBR trades at a lower forward price-to-earnings ratio than its industry, ExxonMobil and Chevron. Put simply, investors pay less for each dollar of Petrobras’ expected earnings. That makes the stock worth considering after its rally. The discount needs context. Petrobras is state-controlled, which creates a risk that government priorities influence business decisions. A cheaper earnings multiple is attractive only if investors are comfortable with those risks and the earnings used to calculate it. Petrobras raised its annual cash investment forecast to $21-$22 billion from $16.9 billion. Its manageable operating expense forecast increased to $24.2–$25.5 billion from $20.2 billion. Management nevertheless expects those expenses per barrel to fall 2% from 2025. Higher lease payments also use cash. Investors comparing Petrobras with ExxonMobil and Chevron should consider how much remains for shareholders after investment and other commitments. Net debt fell to $57.8 billion. Fitch raised Petrobras’ standalone credit profile to bbb+, although its global rating remained BB. The Amapá discovery may offer future resources, but commercial development is uncertain. The agreement to buy the remaining Logum stake also awaits approvals, and its logistics benefits are expected ahead. PBR looks like a buy for investors willing to accept oil-price swings and the risks of state control. Higher production and expected earnings growth support that view, while the valuation remains below peers despite the rally. Rising spending deserves attention because higher operating cash flow does not automatically mean more money for shareholders. On balance, the price and earnings outlook favor buying over selling or waiting. Petrobras stock is currently a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). title: Greg Abel's Berkshire Hathaway Still Holds About $18.6 Billion of Chevron Stock After Selling More Than a Third of It - The Globe and Mail
content: Berkshire Hathaway trimmed its stake in Chevron at the beginning of 2026. But it’s still holding Chevron as its top energy investment. In the first quarter of 2026, Berkshire Hathaway(NYSE: BRKA)(NYSE: BRKB) sold 35% of its position in Chevron (NYSE: CVX), one of the world's largest integrated energy companies. But it increased its position by nearly 7% again in the second quarter, and left it unchanged in the third quarter. As of this writing, Berkshire still holds $18.6 billion in Chevron shares. That's equivalent to a 4.3% stake in Chevron. It accounts for 5% of Berkshire's portfolio, and it's the company's sixth-largest stock investment. Is that a bullish signal for Chevron's future? Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again.In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » Chevron owns upstream, midstream, and downstream assets. However, it generates most of its profits from its upstream extraction business, which benefits the most from rising oil prices. It has a presence in 180 countries, but it still gets most of its oil and natural gas from the U.S., Kazakhstan, and Australia. It has less exposure to the Middle East than many of its big oil peers. Chevron expects to increase its oil and gas production by 2%-3% annually through 2030. That growth will be driven by the expansion of its Tengiz Field in Kazakhstan, drilling upgrades for its largest field in the Permian Basin, its deepwater projects in the Gulf of Mexico, and its increased exposure to Guyana, one of the world's fastest-growing oil regions, through its takeover of Hess. Chevron's stock has rallied more than 40% over the past 12 months. Most of that rally was fueled by rising oil prices after the outbreak of the Iran war in late February. However, Chevron can still easily cover its capex and dividends as long as Brent crude oil -- currently at $95 -- remains above its corporate breakeven price of $50 per barrel. That's why Chevron has raised its dividend annually for 39 consecutive years, and why it has a clear path toward achieving the 50 straight dividend hikes that would make it a Dividend King. Berkshire's new CEO, Greg Abel, was previously the CEO of Berkshire Hathaway Energy. Even though Abel isn't a celebrated stock picker like Warren Buffett, it would make sense for Abel to keep Berkshire exposed to the broader energy market through Chevron. From 2025 to 2028, analysts expect Chevron's revenue and EPS to grow at CAGRs of 5% and 26%, respectively, even if the Iran war ends and oil prices normalize. Those are stellar growth rates for a stock that trades at 14 times next year's earnings and pays a forward yield of 3.2%. That's probably why Abel kept Chevron as a top position in Berkshire's portfolio, even though it shrewdly reduced that position to more balanced levels at the beginning of the year. With ImmunityBio (IBRX) shares up more than 200% this year, founder Patrick Soon-Shiong has outlined plans to unveil decades of privately funded research at NantWorks over the next 12 months, spanning cancer therapies, AI chips and satellite tech. IBRX stock tumbled 9% on Thursday to $6.07, with shares down 30% for the week and tracking their worst week in nearly two years. Soon-Shiong said on X: “I began the release of our stealth, self-funded programs at Nantworks at a speech at Stanford last night.” NantWorks brings together public and private businesses across healthcare, energy and communications. Soon-Shiong highlighted an antibody search engine he likened to Google, part of an effort to find and treat tumors more precisely. He said that the search engine will use camelid antibodies to make tumors visible on PET scans, then targeting them with radioactive isotopes. The goal is to connect cancer detection with treatment directed at the tumor. He also outlined a system that gives doctors real-time patient data to help them make timely treatment decisions. Soon-Shiong said the tech already had FDA approval, but did not name the product. Meanwhile, Soon-Shiong outlined tech to move data faster as AI systems grow. These include high-speed WiGig wireless tech and optical chips that transmit data using light. He also highlighted U.S. factories to make optical chips and chipsets that connect AI data centers. NantOptiFab is already working in this area, making chips in California that use light to carry information for AI networks, space systems and quantum technology. An SEC filing in August named Soon-Shiong as a director and showed that the company raised $20 million by selling shares to one unnamed investor. His space ambitions include chips for use in space, satellite terminals that communicate using light, and new ways to build and launch satellites. The projects also extend to energy, materials and food safety. Soon-Shiong listed batteries that work in Arctic conditions, non-toxic methods of making graphene, biodegradable alternatives to plastic made from ocean-derived materials, and machine vision to detect harmful substances in food and baby food at the point of purchase. Soon-Shiong also spotlighted a blockchain-based exchange for tokenized securities, or digital versions of stocks and other investments. He pitched it as a way to give companies and investors more control. In January, Nant Global Finance announced plans to bring stock trading, shareholder records and blockchain settlement onto one platform. Its acquisitions included Horizon Globex, which provides technology for the Upstream exchange, and BlockAgent and Equity Stock Transfer, which maintain shareholder records. The company also planned to rename Arkonis Capital, a brokerage and trading platform, NantX. At the time, completing its brokerage acquisitions still required approval from the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA). The company is testing whether it can help patients whose immune-cell counts are too low, a condition called lymphopenia. This also includes a sepsis trial that Soon-Shiong said had been authorized. “Trials will be starting soon in USA and Europe,” he said on Wednesday. The Phase 2 study will test Anktiva in about 50 critically ill adults with sepsis and low immune-cell counts. Researchers will compare the drug plus standard care with standard care alone to see whether it reduces deaths within 28 days. “Longevity at work. Book of our patients’ stories soon,” Soon-Shiong said. The drug is already approved in the U.S. with BCG for certain bladder cancers. ImmunityBio’s approval last month expanded its use to another group of patients whose cancer had not responded to BCG. The update comes shortly after ImmunityBio’s third-quarter results, which showed that net product revenue rose 53% from a year earlier to $48.7 million. For the first nine months, it grew 92% to $143.6 million. The company also said its Quilt-2.005 trial met its main goal in a group of bladder cancer patients who had not previously received BCG. Shares of Sellas Life Sciences (SLS) surged 17% in after-hours trading on Thursday after the company said that its key leukemia trial results are expected this month, with its CEO pointing to the treatment’s potential to become a “transformative” immunotherapy if successful. SLS stock fell nearly 5% on Thursday to $8.03, with shares on track to post their third straight weekly decline. The update is related to the Phase 3 Regal trial of Galinpepimut-S (GPS) in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). The November timeline narrows Sellas’ earlier guidance for results in the fourth quarter. “In our ongoing Phase 3 REGAL trial of GPS, we are focused on completing the final analysis following the announcement of 80th event, and we expect to announce topline primary endpoint results this month,” CEO Angelos Stergiou said. “If successful, we believe GPS could be a transformative new immunotherapy for AML patients in second complete remission.” Regal is testing GPS as a maintenance treatment for AML patients who have returned to remission after treatment for a relapse. The study’s main goal is to determine whether GPS helps these patients live longer. GPS is licensed from Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center and targets WT1, a protein found in a range of cancers. Sellas disclosed late last month that the trial had reached its prespecified 80th death, the milestone required to begin its final analysis. This process involves finalizing and reviewing the trial database, revealing treatment assignments and analyzing the results. Beyond GPS, Sellas is advancing its second leukemia drug, Tambiciclib, or SLS009, with investors looking ahead to fresh trial results and a major medical conference presentation. The company has enrolled 40 patients in its planned 80-patient Phase 2 study in newly diagnosed AML, up from 28 disclosed in August. The study includes patients whose disease stops responding early to Azacitidine and Venetoclax, an existing drug combination. Enrollment and treatment are currently continuing, with preliminary results expected in the fourth quarter. The development comes after a completed Phase 2 study in patients whose leukemia returned or failed to respond after prior Venetoclax-based treatment. Sellas will present the findings on Dec.14 at the American Society of Hematology (ASH) meeting in New Orleans. The study enrolled 62 patients and combined SLS009 with azacitidine and venetoclax. Across all doses, 34% of the 59 patients evaluated responded to treatment. At the dose of 30 milligrams twice weekly, 54% of patients with monocytic AML, a leukemia subtype, responded, with median survival of 5.8 months. Among patients with a TP53 mutation, 57% responded, with median survival of 8.8 months. Sellas ended September with $134.7 million in cash and cash equivalents, down from $138.3 million in June. “With $134.7 million in cash and cash equivalents as of September 30, we are well positioned to further advance these programs,” Stergiou said. Third-quarter (Q3) net loss widened to $10.1 million from $6.8 million a year earlier, while loss per share narrowed to $0.05 from $0.06. Meanwhile, research and development spending rose to $7 million from $4.2 million as Sellas prepared for a potential GPS approval application after Regal’s final analysis. Additionally, Sellas is preparing to study SLS009 in pancreatic cancer patients after laboratory findings presented in September. Working with the University of Wisconsin-Madison, researchers tested SLS009 in cancer models grown from patient tissue, including one resistant to Daraxonrasib. They also tested it alongside the experimental drug ZEN3694. Sellas said that the findings support further research into overcoming treatment resistance. However, patient trials are yet to begin.
